segments.text: Welcome to your daily robotics digest for September 25th, 2026.
Today we're diving into open source AI, helpful robots, and exciting educational builds.
Tune in for the updates.
From Robohub, "An open source approach to physical AI from Intrinsic"
details the release of components from Google's Intrinsic platform, aiming to enable the construction of sophisticated robotic applications through adaptable components.

Intrinsic Core includes functionalities such as intrinsic control, pose estimation, motion planning, and grasp planning, alongside the inclusion of Intrinsic-ROS drivers and the Open Machine Tending Solution reference design.
This open source release provides developers with foundational tools to customize their own physical AI solutions by offering starting points for building advanced robotic systems.
The availability of these components facilitates the development of more accessible and customizable physical AI systems across the development community.
This development suggests a push toward democratizing access to advanced robotics development tools.
From Robohub, "Robot Talk Episode 163 – Robots helping people, with Aaron Edsinger"
reports on Stretch robots designed to assist individuals with mobility issues to enhance their independence.
The discussion featured Aaron Edsinger, CEO and Co-Founder of Hello Robot, an organization focused on developing practical, safe, and accessible robots.
Edsinger possesses a background in robotics development at Google and has founded several companies within the robotics sector.
The episode explored the landscape of robotics, artificial intelligence, and autonomous machines.
The Stretch robots focus on providing mobility assistance, demonstrating a practical application of robotics in addressing real-world accessibility challenges.
This work highlights the ongoing development of assistive technology through robotics.
Future developments in this field will continue to shape the intersection of AI and human-robot interaction.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Mexican EPICS in IEEE Team Builds Portable Educational Platform".
This story details the development of a portable educational platform by a team from Mexican EPICS in IEEE, resulting in a functional robotics tool.
The project involved high-school students engaging in hands-on robotics lessons through the development and testing of a system named RoboMeshA.
This work was a collaboration between members of the EPICS in IEEE project and ITESO's Applied Professional Projects program, conducted in partnership with ITESO/Universidad Jesuita de Guadalajara.
The process involved participants actively engaging in the development and testing phases of the platform before its deployment.
This collaborative effort demonstrates the successful integration of advanced robotics education within academic settings.
Future developments in applied robotics education warrant continued attention from the technology sector.
And that's all the circuits for today!
Diving into open source physical AI is a mind-blowing journey.
Thanks for powering up your curiosity.
Until tomorrow, keep building!
